headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: mem0 can ingest PDF-derived content from pdf.js, but both profiles show no network egress and no shared write surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may consume text, while pdf.js processes PDF files and can surface document content. No shared channel or automatic instruction parser is documented, so the pathway is indirect and likely requires manual copy/paste or orchestration. Because uncertainty remains and the rubric says to escalate when unsure, low is the safest choice.
conditions: IF an operator copies PDF text from pdf.js into mem0 as trusted instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator forwards pdf.js output into mem0 without provenance filtering, the risk increases.
mitigations: Treat all PDF-derived text as untrusted input.
Add a provenance tag before passing content from pdf.js to mem0.
Use a human review step for any instruction-like text extracted from PDFs.
Restrict mem0 to summaries, not raw document text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or prompt-separation middleware.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents show network_egress:none, and pdf.js only touches PDF files while mem0 lists no data classes touched. A shared workspace is not documented, so leakage is not established. The main plausible path is local file exposure or manual transfer, which keeps blast radius small and makes low appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory, PDF contents may be visible to both.
IF an operator pastes PDF text into mem0, that content can be retained there.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories for each agent.
Avoid placing sensitive PDFs in shared folders.
Disable any manual export of PDF text into mem0 unless necessary.
Review mem0 memory entries before persistence.
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem isolation between the agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no filesystem write, network, or OAuth scopes in the profile, while pdf.js has browser-based tests and supports multiple instances but no mutable shared-resource write surface is documented. Without overlapping write capabilities, the pairwise conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF mem0 is later configured with filesystem or database writes to the same directory as pdf.js, conflict risk would change.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to one mutable resource, contention could emerge.
mitigations: Keep mem0 read-only in this pairing.
Do not share writable directories between the agents.
Run pdf.js instances in isolated worker contexts.
Document any future shared mutable resource before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: pdf.js can produce extracted document text, and mem0 can store or reuse that content as memory. If mem0's output is later treated as authoritative, errors or hallucinated summaries can cascade into downstream decisions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed into mem0 without verification, incorrect document interpretations can persist.
IF downstream automation trusts mem0 memory entries as facts, errors can propagate.
mitigations: Verify extracted text against the source PDF before storing it.
Mark mem0 entries as untrusted until reviewed.
Require citations back to the original PDF page.
Use a second-pass checker for critical facts.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before mem0 persistence.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent. mem0 lists no touched data classes, and pdf.js only lists PDF documents with no compliance-specific constraints. With no evidence of a compliance boundary, the pairwise compliance risk is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into the workflow, compliance review would be needed.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy not shown in the profiles, reassessment is required.
mitigations: Confirm the data class before processing PDFs.
Keep regulated documents out of this pair until policies are reviewed.
Record retention settings for any stored mem0 memory.
requires-engineering: map deployment regions and compliance controls.
